source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: How does the census support sample surveys within the national statistical system, as described in the passage?
options: It supplies real‑time data that allow surveys to be adjusted on the fly
It eliminates the need for any other data sources in survey design
It defines the questionnaire content for all sample surveys
It provides the sampling frame and population benchmarks used by the surveys
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says that census statistics are used "as a sampling frame for sample surveys" and that they serve as population benchmarks, making option A the correct description.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the passage, which pair of elements is described as indispensable for achieving efficient and reliable data collection in surveys, even when non‑traditional data sources are increasingly available?
options: Multiple field investigators and manual data entry systems
Extensive use of non‑traditional data sources and real‑time analytics
Large sample sizes and advanced statistical software
A sampling frame and population benchmarks derived from the 1860 International Statistics Congress report
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that without the sampling frame and population benchmarks derived from the 1860 report, surveys cannot be efficient and reliable, regardless of the availability of non‑traditional data sources.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: The historical document cited in the passage was printed by which of the following publishers?
options: George Edward Eyre and William Spottiswoode
questions.explanation: The passage identifies the printers of the report as George Edward Eyre and William Spottiswoode, London, 1861.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the timing and venue of the International Statistics Congress whose proceedings are referenced in the passage?
options: It was held in London, beginning on July 16th, 1860 and continued for the five following days.
It was convened in Paris, starting on June 10th, 1859 and lasted a week.
It took place in New York, commencing on August 1st, 1861 and ran for three days.
It occurred in Berlin, beginning on September 5th, 1862 and extended over four days.
questions.explanation: The passage specifies that the Fourth Session of the International Statistics Congress was held in London on July 16th, 1860 and the five following days.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: What digit is presented in the training material?
questions.explanation: The only content provided is the character "2", which is the digit two.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the passage, what is a basic function of a census?
options: Generate statistics on small areas and small population groups
Determine tax rates for each household
Provide real‑time data for daily decision making
Replace all surveys with a single data source
questions.explanation: The text states that a basic function of a census is to generate statistics on small areas and small population groups.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: How can census data be used when planning the location of a school, as described in the material?
options: By mapping the existing road network only
By giving the national average income for the country
By estimating future population growth without regard to age groups
By providing the distribution of school‑age children by school area
questions.explanation: The passage gives the example that planning a school location requires data on the distribution of school‑age children by school area, which may not match administrative boundaries.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Why is census data described as a versatile feature for private‑sector applications?
options: It is always provided free of cost to businesses
It can be tabulated for any geographic unit, allowing flexible statistics
It provides daily updates on population movements
It includes detailed financial information of every household
questions.explanation: The text explains that because census data can be tabulated for any geographic unit, it offers remarkable flexibility, which is valuable for business planning and market analyses.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the primary method many countries use to assemble detailed statistics for small areas and small population groups?
options: Universal and simultaneous individual enumeration of each set of living quarters and each individual
Sampling surveys conducted on a subset of households
questions.explanation: The text explains that many countries achieve detailed statistics by conducting a population and housing census through universal and simultaneous individual enumeration of every living quarter and every individual within the country’s boundaries.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which group is explicitly listed in the passage as a small population group for which accurate census statistics are essential?
questions.explanation: The passage specifically mentions "people with disabilities" (along with ethnic minorities, indigenous peoples, and migrants) as a small population group needing accurate census statistics. The other options are not mentioned.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which statement most accurately reflects the definition of a population census as presented in the material?
options: It focuses exclusively on sampling techniques to infer population characteristics.
It consists solely of gathering demographic data at the national level once every decade.
It involves planning, collecting, processing, analysing, disseminating and evaluating demographic, economic and social data at the smallest geographic level for all persons at a specified time.
It is a periodic survey that estimates economic activity in urban centres only.
questions.explanation: Definition 1.4 describes a population census as the total process of planning, collecting, processing, analysing, disseminating and evaluating demographic, economic and social data at the smallest geographic level for all persons at a specified time.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Why does the passage label the population census as a primary source of basic benchmark statistics?
options: Because it concentrates exclusively on economic indicators at the state level.
Because it supplies reliable and detailed data on the size, distribution and composition of the population needed for economic and social development, administration or research.
Because it is conducted annually across all districts.
Because it provides real‑time data on migration flows.
questions.explanation: Statement 1.5 explains that reliable and detailed data on size, distribution and composition of the population are necessary for planning and research, and the census is the primary source of these benchmark statistics.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which of the following groups are explicitly mentioned as being covered by the population census?
options: Settled population, homeless persons and nomadic groups
questions.explanation: The text states that the population census covers "not only the settled population but also homeless persons and nomadic groups," indicating all three groups are included.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a housing census as defined in the passage?
options: To collect data on the number and condition of housing units and facilities
To count the number of people in a country
questions.explanation: The definition of a housing census in the text describes it as the process of handling statistical data "relating to the number and condition of housing units and facilities".

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the passage, data from the population census can be used in the housing census analysis when:
options: The two censuses are conducted in different years
There is no link between them
Only when housing data is missing
Both operations are conducted together or there is a link between them
questions.explanation: The text notes that data from the population census, including data on homeless persons, are often used in housing‑census results "if both operations are conducted together or there is a link between them."

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a key feature of population and housing censuses?
questions.explanation: The key features listed in the material are individual enumeration, universality within a defined territory, simultaneity, defined periodicity, and the capacity to produce small‑area statistics. Continuous data collection is not among them.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: The requirement of individual enumeration can be satisfied by which of the following approaches?
options: Use of an appropriate administrative register only
A combination of field collection and registers
questions.explanation: The text states that individual enumeration can be met by collection of information in the field (face‑to‑face interviews or self‑response), by the use of information contained in an appropriate administrative register or set of registers, or by a combination of these methods. Hence all three options are valid.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the material, data on homeless persons are incorporated into the housing census analysis under which condition?
options: Only when a separate homelessness survey is carried out
When the population and housing censuses are conducted together or linked
questions.explanation: The passage notes that data on homeless persons are used in the presentation and analysis of the housing census "if both operations are conducted together or there is a link between them."

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the passage, how is the "census day" defined in relation to the actual enumeration process?
options: It is defined as the day when the census results are officially published.
It may be a reference date that precedes the period of field enumeration.
It is always set after the completion of data processing to reflect final results.
It must be the exact calendar day on which every household is visited.
questions.explanation: The text states that the census day "may be a period prior to the census," indicating that it can serve as a reference date before the actual enumeration.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which of the following reasons does the passage give for a country to conduct censuses more frequently than the recommended ten‑year interval?
options: To reduce the cost of using administrative records.
Because of rapid changes in the population and/or its housing circumstances.
To align census data with the national budget cycle.
To comply with international treaty obligations.
questions.explanation: The passage notes that "some countries may find it necessary to carry out censuses more frequently because of the rapidity of major changes in their population and/or its housing circumstances."

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: What potential benefit of using data derived from administrative sources is mentioned in the passage?
options: It guarantees higher accuracy than field enumeration.
It enables the production of statistical outputs at shorter intervals.
It eliminates the requirement for a defined census day.
It completely replaces the need for a traditional census.
questions.explanation: The passage states that "the use of data derived from administrative sources may provide the opportunity for more frequently produced statistical outputs," indicating a benefit of more frequent releases.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the passage, why should countries aim to conduct censuses in years ending in “0”?
options: Because it is required by the United Nations.
To avoid conflicts with national elections.
To coincide with fiscal year budgeting cycles.
To align with international comparability of census data.
questions.explanation: The text states that census data are of greater value if they can be compared with censuses of other countries taken at approximately the same time, so countries should try to undertake a census in years ending in “0”.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: For European Union member countries, what is the mandatory census year pattern?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says, “For EU countries it is mandatory to have censuses in years ending in ‘1’.”

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which of the following is described as an essential feature of censuses that rely on full field enumeration?
options: Including a question on household deaths.
Conducting the census every five years.
questions.explanation: The text notes that “Simultaneity is an essential feature of censuses that rely on full field enumeration (the so‑called traditional approach).”

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: When fixing a census date, which factor may be given greater weight than the desire for international simultaneity?
options: Technological readiness of the census bureau
questions.explanation: The passage states that in fixing a census date, national and regional factors could be given greater weight than the desirability of international simultaneity.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the passage, what is required of census data concerning small population groups and geographic detail?
options: Data should be released without any confidentiality safeguards
Data should be produced down to the lowest appropriate geographic level while protecting confidentiality
Data should exclude housing unit characteristics
Data should be aggregated only at the national level to protect privacy
questions.explanation: The text specifies that the census should produce data on the number and characteristics of the population and housing units down to the lowest appropriate geographic level, compatible with national circumstances, and for small population groups, while protecting confidentiality of personal information.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the passage, which statement best explains why considering the relationships between the population census, the housing census, and other statistical investigations from the outset enhances the census’s benefits?
options: It allows the census to replace the need for any future sample surveys.
It enables the census to directly calculate vital rates without civil registration data.
It ensures that the census data can serve as a statistical frame and share consistent concepts, maximizing shared purposes.
It reduces the cost of the census by eliminating the housing census.
questions.explanation: The passage states that when the relationships between the population census, the housing census and other statistical investigations are considered from the outset, their shared purposes can best be served and benefits harnessed, and that consistent concepts and definitions throughout an integrated programme are essential. This matches option C.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: The passage mentions that census‑type information can be obtained without a complete enumeration. Which alternative sources are explicitly identified?
options: Satellite imagery and remote sensing data.
Administrative tax records and school enrollment lists.
Household utility bills and mobile phone usage logs.
questions.explanation: The text explicitly says that census‑type information can be derived from population registers and can also be estimated from sample surveys without undertaking a complete enumeration. The other options are not mentioned.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the role of the population census in calculating vital rates is supported by the passage?
options: The population census alone provides all necessary data for vital rates, making civil registration data redundant.
Housing census data are the primary source for vital rates, while the population census is used only for social indicators.
Vital rates are calculated exclusively from sample surveys, with the census serving only as a backup.
Population estimates derived from the census are combined with civil registration data to calculate vital rates.
questions.explanation: The passage notes that the population census is important in developing the population estimates needed to calculate vital rates in combination with civil registration data. This corresponds to option D.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes alternative sources that can provide census‑type information without a complete enumeration?
options: Only population registers can be used.
Both population registers and sample surveys can be used.
Only sample surveys can be used.
Neither population registers nor sample surveys can be used.
questions.explanation: The passage states that census‑type information can be derived from population registers and can also be estimated from sample surveys without undertaking a complete enumeration, indicating that both sources are viable alternatives.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Why must census offices produce relevant data according to the text?
options: To support countries in tracking progress toward internationally agreed development agendas such as the 2030 Agenda and its Sustainable Development Goals.
To replace the need for sample surveys entirely.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1.17 explains that data are required to measure and monitor indicators for the 2030 Agenda and SDGs, and therefore census offices must produce the relevant data to meet these commitments.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: In what ways do population and housing censuses aid environmental and disaster‑management efforts, as described in the passage?
options: They directly reduce greenhouse‑gas emissions through census activities.
They provide information for analyzing energy consumption, identifying conservation opportunities, forecasting energy needs, and planning relief operations for natural disasters.
They map geological fault lines for earthquake prediction.
They fund disaster‑relief operations through census‑generated revenue.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1.18 notes that censuses are a key source of data for environmental statistics, helping agencies analyze energy use, identify conservation options, forecast energy needs, and assist governments and relief agencies in planning operations for disasters such as floods and hurricanes.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: According to the passage, census data help public health authorities primarily by:
questions.explanation: The text states that the census provides a rich source of data for public health authorities in identifying prevalence levels of disease, among other health‑related uses.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: The passage says census data are frequently integrated with other thematic data to:
options: Derive essential indicators for comprehensive analyses
Limit the sharing of information between agencies
Replace the need for any other surveys
Increase the overall cost of data collection
questions.explanation: It explicitly states that integrating census data with other thematic data is done to derive essential indicators for comprehensive analyses.

source.title: Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses, Revision 4

questions.question: Which skill set is explicitly cited in the passage as being enhanced by census work but is not typically prominent in other parts of the National Statistical Office?
questions.explanation: The text lists "project management" among the varied sets of skills required for administering a census that are not necessarily prominent in other parts of the organization.
